name: caldera
description:
(opt18) Name: Caldera
Submitted by: Andy Applebaum, Doug Miller, and Blake Strom from MITRE.

Description: Cybersecurity domain based on the CALDERA project with certain
simplifications like assuming that the network is fully known. Actions are taken from the
MITRE ATT&CK framework which is a taxonomy of attacker behaviors observed in the real
world. The basic paradigm of the included actions is to steal credentials from hosts we
have access to and use them to laterally move across the network, which is representative
of real adversary behavior: many adversaries tend to leverage existing, benign
capabilities for malicious ends, which is in contrast with some threat models that assume
that attackers are exploiting box-to-box. The instances were generated dynamically based
on a simulator that uses a few parameters to emulate a real network. These parameters
control the number of hosts, the number of users, the number of domains, and the
probability of credential overlap among others.

Interesting properties: quantified conditional effects, hard to ground (some action schemas
have 10 parameters or more). To alleviate grounding issues we have two versions of the
domain, one that applies action splitting and one that does not.

Miller, Doug, et al. “Automated Adversary Emulation: A Case for Planning and Acting with Unknowns.” IntEx 2018. Available online at
- https://www.mitre.org/publications/technical-papers/automated-adversary-emulation-a-case-for-planning-and-acting-with
